name: Would a peninsula work better than an island in my small kitchen?

mainEntity.name: Would a peninsula work better than an island in my small kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: A peninsula often provides seating and counter space with less disruption than a freestanding island, but neither is automatically right. A peninsula may preserve a wider central passage and connect the kitchen to an adjoining room, while an island can provide access from multiple sides if the room is wide enough. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare both in a layout visualization using your actual doors, appliances, and traffic paths. Key factors include seating depth, outlet placement, dishwasher clearance, work-zone separation, and the location of the refrigerator. Decide whether seating or preparation space matters more. Avoid adding seating if it blocks the primary route through the home.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often, yes, because a peninsula can add seating and counter space while using less floor area. The better option depends on traffic, appliance clearances, doorway locations, and whether your priority is seating, preparation, or storage.
